chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who catches the second rak'ah of the prayer with the Imam, and it is the first for himself. How should he act when the Imam sits? He (peace be upon him) said: He should sit upright and not sit fixedly. So when the third is for the Imam and it is the second for him, let him wait a little when the Imam stands, for the time it takes to perform the Tashahhud, then he should catch up with the Imam.

He said: And I asked him about the one who catches the last two rak'ahs of the prayer, how should he deal with the recitation? So he (peace be upon him) said: Recite in them, for they are the first two for you, and do not make the beginning of your prayer its end.

key_terms.تَشَهَّد: Tashahhud (testimonies recited during sitting in prayer)
key_terms.قُعُود: Sitting (specifically the sitting between prostrations or before final standing)

ai.seo_question: How should a person adjust their prayer if they join the Imam late and miss the first rak'ah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural nuances for latecomers (muqtadi) joining congregational prayer, emphasizing that the number of rak'ahs caught determines the legal status of those units as either primary or supplementary. It specifically addresses the physical posture during the Imam's sitting and the obligation of recitation in the 'first' rak'ahs of the latecomer, ensuring the validity of the prayer according to Shia fiqh. The ruling underscores the principle that the latecomer's prayer is completed by following the Imam, yet retains independent validity for the units they actively participated in.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who attains the second Rak’at from the Salāt with the Imam, and it is the first for himself. How should he deal with it when the Imam sits?’ Heasws said: ‘He should withdraw and not sit fixedly. So when it was the third (Rak’at) for the Imam and it is the second for him, so let him wait a little when the Imam stands, when he can perform Tashahhud with. The he should catch up with the Imam’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about the one who attains the last two Rak’at from the Salāt, how should they deal with the recitation’. So heasws said: ‘Recite (himself) in these two, for these two would be the first two for you, and not make the beginning of your Salāt to be its end’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who joins the congregation in the second Rak‘at which is the first for him. What is he to do when the Imam sits down? He (the Imam) said, ‘He displays readiness to stand up (by raising his knees from the ground and placing his palms on the ground), does not allow himself to sit down. When it is the third Rak‘at for the Imam and the second for him, he waits a little while to say Tashahhud (testimonies of belief), then joins the Imam?

He (the narrator) has said that he then asked him (the Imam) about one who joins a congregation in the two last Rak‘at of Salah (prayer) and what is one to do about recitation. He (the Imam) said, ‘Recite in them; they are the first two Rak‘at for you and do not make the beginning of your Salah (prayer) its end.’”
